exercises.title: U5 听力·对话 Joining the Nature Club
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Mia: Leo, the nature club is looking for volunteers this weekend. Want to join?
Leo: Maybe. What would we actually be doing?
Mia: We'd help clean a small lake and plant trees along the bank.
Leo: That sounds tiring. Why does it matter so much?
Mia: The dirty water is driving the birds away. Clean water brings them back.
Leo: I see. So we're really helping the whole habitat, not just the lake.
Mia: Exactly. And the club will teach us how to record the birds we see.
Leo: All right, count me in. It feels good to do something real.
exercises.translation_cn: Mia 邀 Leo 周末做自然俱乐部志愿者;任务是清理小湖、在岸边种树;Leo 问为何重要;Mia 说脏水赶走了鸟,清水能让鸟回来;Leo 明白这是在帮整个栖息地;俱乐部还会教他们记录看到的鸟;Leo 答应参加。

questions.stem: Why does the work matter, according to Mia?
options: The dirty water is driving the birds away.

options: How to record the birds they see.

exercises.title: U5 听力·短文 Saving the Wild Tiger
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: The wild tiger is one of the most beautiful animals on Earth, but it is also in great danger.
A hundred years ago, many thousands of tigers lived in the forests of Asia.
Today only a few thousand remain.
People have cut down the forests where tigers hunt, leaving them with less space and less food.
To save the tiger, several countries have set up special reserves where the animals are protected, and in some of these places tiger numbers are slowly rising again.
exercises.translation_cn: 野生老虎美丽,却也处境危险;一百年前亚洲森林里有成千上万只老虎;如今只剩几千只;人们砍掉了老虎捕猎的森林,使它们空间和食物变少;为拯救老虎,一些国家设立了保护区,在部分地区老虎数量正缓慢回升。

questions.stem: What is happening to the wild tiger?

Why do tigers now have less food and space?
options: Their forests have been cut down.

questions.stem: What have several countries done to help?
What is happening in some of the reserves?

exercises.title: U5 听力·对话 A Visit to the Reserve
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Visitor: Excuse me, is it true that this island once had almost no birds left?
Guide: Not quite. Long ago it was full of seabirds, until people brought rats and cats.
Visitor: And those animals attacked the birds?
Guide: Yes. The number of native birds fell very quickly.
Visitor: So what did people do to put it right?
Guide: They spent years removing the rats and cats, using traps and trained dogs.
Visitor: That must have been hard work.
Guide: It was. But now the seabirds are nesting here again, and the island is finally safe.
exercises.translation_cn: 游客问这座岛是否曾几乎没有鸟了;导游说从前满是海鸟,直到有人带来老鼠和猫;那些动物袭击了鸟;本地鸟数量骤降;人们花了数年用陷阱和受训的狗清除老鼠和猫;虽然辛苦,但如今海鸟重新筑巢,岛终于安全了。

questions.stem: What was the island once full of?
What caused the bird numbers to fall?
options: Rats and cats brought by people.

questions.stem: How did people remove the rats and cats?
options: By using a strong poison only.
By waiting for them to leave.

questions.stem: How long did the work take?
What are the seabirds doing now?

exercises.title: U5 听力·短文 Trees in the City
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Trees do far more for a city than make it look pretty.
On a hot day, the shade under a tree can be several degrees cooler than the open street.
Trees also clean the air by taking in harmful gases and giving out fresh oxygen.
Their roots hold the soil and soak up rainwater, which helps to stop floods.
Birds and insects find food and shelter among the branches, so many cities are now planting more trees along their streets and in their parks.
exercises.translation_cn: 树木对城市的作用远不止美观;炎热天树荫比空旷街道凉好几度;树净化空气,吸入有害气体、释放新鲜氧气;树根固土、吸收雨水,有助防洪;鸟和昆虫在枝间觅食栖身,因此许多城市正沿街道和公园多种树。

questions.stem: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Trees do much more than make a city pretty.

questions.stem: How does a tree help on a hot day?
options: Its shade keeps the area cooler.

questions.stem: How do trees help the air?
options: They add dust to the air.

questions.stem: How do tree roots help stop floods?
options: They hold soil and soak up rainwater.

exercises.title: U5 听力·对话 Cutting Down on Plastic
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Anna: I read that millions of sea animals die each year because of plastic. It's awful.
Tom: I know. I saw a photo of a turtle caught in a plastic bag.
Anna: We use so much plastic without thinking. Maybe we should cut down.
Tom: Good idea. I could bring my own cloth bag when I go shopping.
Anna: And I'll carry a metal bottle instead of buying plastic ones.
Tom: Small changes, but if everyone did them, they would really help.
Anna: Let's also tell our classmates. The more people join, the bigger the difference.
Tom: Agreed. Protecting the sea starts with what we do every day.
exercises.translation_cn: Anna 读到每年数百万海洋动物因塑料死亡,感到痛心;Tom 见过被塑料袋困住的海龟;两人决定减少用塑料;Tom 购物自带布袋;Anna 用金属瓶代替塑料瓶;小改变若人人都做就有大用;他们还要告诉同学,人越多差别越大;保护海洋从日常做起。

questions.stem: Why do millions of sea animals die each year?
What did Tom see in a photo?
options: A bird in a tall tree.
A fish in a clean river.
A turtle caught in a plastic bag.

questions.stem: What will Tom do when he goes shopping?
What will Anna use instead of plastic bottles?
What do they decide to ask their classmates to do?
options: To stay away from the sea.

exercises.title: U5 听力·短文 A Tip for Helping Birds
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Here is a simple way to help the wild birds near your home.
In winter, food can be hard for them to find, so you can hang a small feeder in your garden or on your balcony.
Keep it filled with seeds and clean water, and the birds will soon come to visit.
Try not to make loud noises that might frighten them away.
Planting a few native bushes also gives them a safe place to rest, so with just a little effort you can turn your home into a friendly stop for the birds.
exercises.translation_cn: 这里有个帮助家附近野鸟的简单方法;冬天它们难觅食,可在花园或阳台挂个小喂食器;装满种子和干净的水,鸟很快就会来;别发出可能吓走它们的大声;种几丛本地灌木也能给它们安全的歇息处,只需一点努力,家就能成为鸟儿友好的歇脚地。

questions.stem: Who is this tip mainly for?
options: People who want to help wild birds.

options: Making loud noises that frighten the birds.
